profile.reading: This H5 Data Centers facility is located at 100 Taylor Street, San Antonio, Texas 78205. The operator own facility page states 85,000 square feet of colocation space across 2 facilities at this address, with 2N UPS power, 48 hour diesel runtime generator backup, and N+1 chillers, cooling towers, and CRAHs. The facility connects to 35 on net carriers with dark fiber and 100 Gbps options. No MW capacity figure is published for this specific building. H5 Data Centers is a privately held US colocation and wholesale data center operator with facilities spanning roughly two dozen markets nationwide, per the company's own site, of which this San Antonio facility is one. Downtown San Antonio has developed a modest but real colocation and network-interconnection cluster over the past two decades, drawing on the city's position as a South Texas hub for enterprise, healthcare, and military-adjacent IT demand from nearby installations, distinct from the much larger hyperscale build-out underway elsewhere in Central Texas. H5 markets this facility for its carrier density, citing 35 on-net carriers with dark fiber and 100 Gbps options as a draw for customers needing redundant, low-latency connectivity in the South Texas market. H5 is not a publicly traded company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's power, cooling, and certification details are sourced solely to the operator's own published facility page rather than an independently corroborating source, a limitation this registry notes rather than treats as disqualifying, consistent with its general practice for privately held colocation operators. The operator's own page describes 85,000 square feet of colocation space split across 2 facilities at this one address without breaking the total down further, so this entry records the combined figure rather than guessing an individual-building split; no year-opened date or third-party audited capacity figure was located this session.

reading.body:
H5 Data Centers San Antonio operates 85,000 square feet of colocation space across two facilities at a single address in downtown San Antonio. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this campus. Without a power specification, the scale of this site relative to the state's mapped data center infrastructure cannot be assessed from published sources.

The facility qualifies to host SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliant workloads. Redundancy is specified as 2N UPS backup, N+1 cooling and generator support with 48 hours of diesel runtime. The campus connects to 35 carrier networks including dark fiber and 100 Gbps options, indicating connectivity sufficient for multi-tenant enterprise use but not optimized for the sustained single-tenant power draws typical of AI training clusters.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities and 468 MW of published capacity spread across 18 of them. H5 San Antonio ranks 19th among Texas facilities by published megawatt capacity, which means it either publishes no figure or publishes below the threshold of the 18th-ranked site. The absence of any MW disclosure from the operator's spec page places this campus outside the set of facilities with quantifiable power constraints or scaling potential as measured by this site's methodology.
